webcal.title: Webcal
webcal.desc: A calendar address, such as a webcal:// link from Google, iCloud, Proton, Outlook or Nextcloud. Import copies the events one time. Subscribe shows them in your calendar, read-only, and keeps them up to date while the app is open.
webcal.subscribeDesc: Paste a calendar address, such as a webcal:// link from Google, iCloud, Proton, Outlook or Nextcloud. Its events show in your calendar, read-only, and update while the app is open.

errors.invalid: Paste an address that starts with webcal://, webcals:// or https://.
errors.wrongType: This address does not lead to a calendar file.
errors.tooLarge: This calendar is larger than 10 MB.
errors.timeout: The calendar server did not answer in time. Try again later.
errors.blocked: The calendar server refused the download. Check that the calendar is shared or public.
errors.offline: You are offline. Connect and try again.
errors.limit: Too many downloads in a short time. Wait a minute and try again.
errors.failed: The calendar could not be downloaded. Check the address and try again.
errors.full: You can subscribe to {{max}} calendars at most. Remove one first.

sourceDesc.googleKeep: Google Takeout .zip (Keep folder) or a single .json note. Checklists import as native task lists.
sourceDesc.googleCalendar: The .zip from Google Calendar's Settings > Import & export, or one .ics file. Events keep their times, repeats and reminders.
sourceDesc.appleNotes: Export via the free Exporter app as Markdown, then drop the .zip here.
sourceDesc.appleJournal: Export from Journal on Mac or iPhone, compress the AppleJournalEntries folder, and drop the .zip. Entries import as journal entries with their photos, videos, voice memos, and locations.
sourceDesc.excalidraw: Drawings saved from excalidraw.com: one .excalidraw file, or several zipped together. Drawings from Obsidian's Excalidraw plugin work too, as .excalidraw.md files. Pictures inside a drawing come along.
sourceDesc.evernote: One .enex on its own, or several zipped together. Keeps formatting, tags, attachments, note links, and notebooks. Evernote leaves tasks out of .enex.
sourceDesc.samsungNotes: Export as Word (.docx) or Text (.txt). Zip multiple files for bulk import.
sourceDesc.simplenote: Export from Simplenote (Settings -> Tools -> Export Notes). Drop the .zip.
sourceDesc.standardNotes: Decrypted .zip or .txt backup from Standard Notes (Account settings > Backups > Data backups > Decrypted).
sourceDesc.obsidian: Obsidian vault as .zip. Preserves tags, note-links, folder structure, inline #tags, and embedded images and files. Canvases and Excalidraw drawings become drawings, and one .canvas file imports on its own too.
sourceDesc.obsidianCanvas: One .canvas file from your Obsidian vault, or the whole vault as a .zip to bring in every canvas. Each canvas becomes a drawing: cards, groups, arrows and colors come along, and pictures do too when they are in the .zip.
sourceDesc.notesnook: Notesnook export as .zip. Pick HTML when exporting to keep formatting, notebooks, tags, and attachments.
sourceDesc.bear: In Bear, choose File > Backup Notes... and drop the .bear2bk file here. Tags and nested tags, pins, the archive, the trash, highlights with their colors, note-links and attachments come along.
sourceDesc.joplin: The .jex file from File > Export all > "JEX - Joplin Export File". Notebooks become folders, and tags, to-dos, note links and attachments come along.
sourceDesc.upnote: In UpNote: Settings > Backup > Backup now, then zip everything in the backup folder. Keeps notebooks, tags, pins, note links, formatting, and attachments. Per-note exports from the phone apps work too - pick "Export to HTML".
sourceDesc.markdownFolder: .md or .txt files individually or as a .zip. A zipped folder keeps its subfolders and brings its images and attachments along.
sourceDesc.markdownApp: These notes are already Markdown files in a folder. Drop that folder in as a .zip and its subfolders, images, and #tags come with it.
sourceDesc.browserBookmarks: The bookmarks .html file from your browser’s "Export bookmarks", or the .zip Safari writes. Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge, Opera, Brave, and Vivaldi all hold the same file. Folders and dates come along.
sourceDesc.vcard: The .vcf file your address book exports: iPhone and Mac through iCloud or Contacts, Android, Google Contacts. Every card comes across, photos included, and importing the same file twice skips the people you already have.
sourceDesc.bitwarden: Unencrypted .json vault export from Bitwarden (Tools > Export vault > .json). Logins, cards, SSH keys, secure notes, and TOTP codes all come along.
sourceDesc.browserPasswords: The passwords .csv from Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi, Firefox, or Safari, or the .zip Safari writes. Each row becomes a login. Delete the file when you are done - it holds your passwords in plain text.

restorePick.intro: Restore a PrivacyNotes backup you exported earlier.
restorePick.fullBackupDesc: Restore notes, journals, vault items, tasks, images, audio, and files. A note you already have is kept, or updated if the backup holds a newer copy of it.
restorePick.encryptedBackupDesc: Restore an encrypted backup with your phrase key. A .pnbackupz brings everything back, files included; a .pnbackup carries text content and metadata only. You must be signed in with the same account that created it.

restoreGate.wait: Restore waits until this device is online and has completed a sync, so your backup is matched to the notes already in your account instead of adding them twice.
restoreGate.paused: Restore waits for sync, so your backup is matched to the notes already in your account, and sync is paused on this device: turn off Pause sync in Settings > ID & Sync.
restoreGate.belowFloor: Restore waits for sync, so your backup is matched to the notes already in your account, and this version of the app is too old to sync: update the app first.

errors.blobsNotInBackup_one: Your notes were restored, but {{items}} listed in the backup is missing from it.
errors.blobsNotInBackup_other: Your notes were restored, but {{items}} listed in the backup are missing from it.

preview.oversize_other: {{count}} notes are over 1 MB. They stay on this device and do not sync.

preview.splitOversize_other: Split these {{count}} notes into smaller notes at their headings, so they sync

preview.oversizeAttachments_other: {{count}} files are larger than the {{limit}} per-file limit on your plan. They import to this device, but they will not sync to your other devices until you upgrade.
preview.title: Check before importing
preview.sourceTagDesc: Off: no tag for the source. Tags already in the notes come along either way.
preview.storageLine: This import needs about {{needed}}. You have {{available}} free.
preview.nothingWritten: Nothing is written until you press Import.

export.intro: Your data is yours. Export any time, for free.
export.manualIntro: A copy of everything, made now. Keep it somewhere safe.
export.zipBackupDesc: Your notes, journals, vault items, tasks, images, audio and files, with your medications and trackers. Opens on any computer with no phrase, so store it somewhere safe. Note History and your app lock PIN are not included.
export.encryptedZipBackupDesc: The same as the zip, sealed with your phrase key. Restores with your phrase on any device. Safe to store anywhere.
export.encryptedBackupDesc: All text content and metadata, with no images or files. A small file, sealed with your phrase key. Safe to store anywhere.
export.notesMarkdownDesc: Only your notes, one Markdown file each, in the same folders as in the app, with their pictures and files. No tasks, journal entries, events or vault items, and nothing from the trash. Not encrypted, so store it somewhere safe.
export.htmlArchiveDesc: One printable HTML page per note, logins, cards and keys included in plain text. Good for reading offline or archiving, not for restoring. Store it somewhere safe.
export.textBackupDesc: All text content and metadata as plain JSON. No images or files. Store somewhere you trust - this is not encrypted.
export.vaultExportDesc: Logins, cards, and SSH keys in Bitwarden-compatible format. Importable by most password managers. Plaintext - handle with care.
export.bookmarksExportDesc: The standard bookmarks file every browser reads. Import it into Chrome, Firefox, Safari, or Edge with your folders intact.
export.contactsExportDesc: The vCard file every phone and address book reads. Import it into iPhone, Android, Google Contacts, or Contacts on the Mac, labels and groups intact.
export.calendarExportDesc: Events and dated notes and task lists, for Google Calendar, Apple Calendar or Outlook.
export.drawingsExportDesc: Every drawing as its own .excalidraw file, pictures inside, for excalidraw.com and Obsidian.

exportProgress.missingFailed_other: This device could not download {{items}}, so your export leaves them out. Check your connection and export again.

exportProgress.missingNotFound_other: {{items}} are not on this device or on the server, so your export leaves them out.

decryptErrors.tooSmall: This file is empty or incomplete ({{size}} bytes), so there is nothing to restore. Export the backup again and check that the saved file has a real size before importing it.

A .pnbackup only opens in the account that created it, so this is usually a backup from a different account - to move notes between accounts, export a full backup (.zip) instead. If it is the right account, the file was damaged or saved incompletely.

saveErrors.protectedFolder: PrivacyNotes does not save into {{folder}}, because that folder holds keys, settings or programs. Save the file somewhere else and move it there yourself.

destination.help: Folders from the source go inside the folder you pick, and items without a folder go into it.

upnote.perNoteMarkdownWarning: This is UpNote's per-note Markdown export. It keeps text, lists, tables, code, math, links, images, and attachments - but UpNote flattens callouts, text colors, alignment, and sub/superscript before writing it, and it carries no notebooks, pins, or original dates. On the phone, "Export to HTML" keeps that formatting; on a computer, Settings > Backup keeps everything.
upnote.perNoteHtmlWarning: These are UpNote's per-note HTML exports: formatting, images, and attachments come across in full. Per-note exports carry no notebooks, pins, or original dates - on a computer, Settings > Backup produces a backup folder that keeps those too.
